name: The Long Dark: Protons and Black Holes

pages.text: If the universe expands forever, its history after the stars falls into eras. The last red dwarfs die after 10¹⁴ years; then the $(thing)Degenerate Era$() of white dwarfs, neutron stars and planets - until, if grand unification is right, $(thing)Proton Decay$() dissolves them: p → e⁺ + π⁰, with a lifetime above 10³⁴ years.
Watch a tank of water long enough, like Super-Kamiokande: in the $(item)Neutrino Condenser$(), Cherenkov quartz and neutronium under 4,000 mB of water catch $(item)Proton Decay Residue$().

Then the $(thing)Black Hole Era$(): only black holes remain, radiating at T = ħc³/(8πGMk_B). A solar-mass hole takes 10⁶⁷ years to evaporate, getting hotter as it shrinks, and ends in a flash. A $(item)Kugelblitz Chamber$() evaporates a micro singularity down to its $(item)Last Flash$().
